title: Model Question Paper 1
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–20 carry 1 mark each; questions 21–35 carry 2 marks each.
Section B: 2-mark answers in 30–50 words, 3-mark answers in 50–80 words, 6-mark answers in 80–120 words. Map questions carry 4 marks.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Why was the Glorious Revolution of 1688 called 'glorious'? Why did King James II lose the support of his countrymen?
questions.answer: It was called glorious because no blood was shed. James II lost support because of his harsh attitude, the expensive standing army he created and his increasing employment of Roman Catholics in government, army and universities. Parliament replaced him with Mary II and William III.

questions.q: Why did Europeans want to trade with the East during the Industrial Revolution?
questions.answer: Factories needed a steady supply of raw materials and new markets to sell their machine-made goods, and capitalists needed places to invest surplus capital. The East was rich in resources and had large populations, so trade there was very profitable.

questions.q: Why has untouchability been made a punishable offence under law in India? Explain.
questions.answer: Untouchability denied millions of people equal status and dignity because of their caste or occupation. To uplift them socially and establish equality, the Constitution abolished it (Article 17) and made its practice in any form a punishable offence.

questions.q: Explain any two qualifications for a Governor of an Indian State.
questions.answer: (1) He/she must be a citizen of India and at least 35 years old. (2) He/she must not hold any office of profit; a member of Parliament, a State Legislature or a Council of Ministers who becomes Governor must give up that seat.

or.q: Explain any two powers of the Chief Minister of a State.
or.answer: (1) He/she forms the Council of Ministers by advising the Governor and allocates and can change portfolios. (2) He/she guides policy-making, presides over cabinet meetings and is the link between the Governor and the Council of Ministers.

questions.q: Explain any two essential conditions for democracy.
questions.answer: (1) A Constitution that vests supreme power in the people and protects rights, with universal adult franchise and regular free elections. (2) Social and economic equality — education for all, social security and the fruits of development reaching the poor; also a responsible government and a free press.

questions.q: Mention any two indicators of socio-economic development.
questions.answer: Any two: per capita income / GDP; literacy rate; life expectancy; level of employment; infant mortality; access to health care.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe the condition of Italy on the eve of the Renaissance in the 14th century.
questions.answer: Italy was divided into small city-states, many built on the ruins of Roman buildings. Cities like Venice were great centres of trade and intellectual crossroads. The new political and social organisation gave freedom and a good atmosphere for academic and artistic advancement. Trade brought wealth, and people had more leisure for study.

questions.q: Explain any three consequences of the Second World War.
questions.answer: (1) It caused unprecedented loss of life and property; Jews were sent to concentration camps, and atomic bombs destroyed Hiroshima and Nagasaki, raising the danger of nuclear war. (2) Germany was divided into four zones and Japan was put under US supervision; imperialism weakened and colonies in Asia and Africa became independent. (3) The USA and USSR emerged as superpowers, the Cold War began, and the United Nations was founded.

questions.q: Explain any three features of the Central Highlands of India.
questions.answer: (1) They lie north of the Narmada, between the river and the Northern Plains. (2) They include the Aravalli range (highest peak Gurushikhar near Mt. Abu), the Malwa plateau (drained by the Betwa, Chambal and Ken) and the Chhota Nagpur plateau (Mahadeo, Kaimur and Maikal hills). (3) The Narmada flows west in a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.

questions.q: Describe any three factors affecting the climate of India.
questions.answer: (1) Latitude: the Tropic of Cancer divides India into a hotter tropical south and a sub-tropical north. (2) Distance from the sea: coastal places have an equable climate, interior places an extreme climate. (3) Mountains: the Himalayas block cold Central Asian winds and trap the monsoon; the Western Ghats cause heavy rain on their windward side. (Altitude, surface winds and jet streams also matter.)

questions.q: How is casteism a challenge to Indian democracy? Explain in three points.
questions.answer: (1) Untouchability and caste discrimination persist despite the constitutional ban, denying Dalits dignity and opportunities. (2) Politicisation of caste and 'casteisation of politics' — parties use caste as vote-banks for narrow gains, weakening issues-based politics. (3) It keeps socio-economic inequalities alive and sometimes causes caste violence, against the democratic ideals of equality and fraternity.

or.q: How is criminalisation of politics a challenge to Indian democracy? Explain in three points.
or.answer: (1) People with criminal records contest and win elections using money and muscle power, negating democratic values. (2) Violence and intimidation stop voters from voting freely and spoil free and fair elections. (3) Criminals in power protect lawbreakers, increase corruption and reduce public trust; courts and alert voters must reject such candidates.

questions.q: Explain any three measures taken by the government for the economic and social empowerment of women.
questions.answer: (1) Poverty eradication and training programmes addressed to women's needs, especially in agriculture. (2) Labour laws, social security and support services such as crèches to help women work in industry. (3) Equal access to education, health and nutrition and elimination of violence against women; politically, one-third reservation in local bodies.

or.q: What is the role of the National Rural Health Mission? Mention any two other health programmes for women and children.
or.answer: Medical facilities are concentrated in cities, so NRHM was launched to provide accessible, affordable health care in rural areas, reducing the rural–urban gap. Other programmes: Janani Suraksha Yojana, Balika Samridhi Yojana, Kishori Shakti Yojana (any two).

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: How did the French Revolution influence the world? Explain its causes and impact.
questions.answer: Causes: (1) French society was divided into three estates; the clergy and nobility enjoyed privileges while the Third Estate (peasants, workers, middle class) bore heavy taxes. (2) Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette's luxury emptied the treasury. (3) In 1789 the Third Estate declared itself the National Assembly. (4) Thinkers like Voltaire, Montesquieu and Rousseau inspired people. Impact: (5) The Declaration of the Rights of Man and Citizen asserted equality, sovereignty of the people and rights to liberty, property and free speech; France became a republic. (6) Its ideals of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity, liberalism and nationalism spread across the world and inspired the unification of Italy.

questions.q: Explain the six Fundamental Rights guaranteed by the Indian Constitution.
questions.answer: (1) Right to Equality (Art. 14–18): equality before law, no discrimination, equal opportunity in jobs, abolition of untouchability and titles. (2) Right to Freedom (Art. 19–22): six freedoms, protection in conviction, life and personal liberty, safeguards on arrest; Article 21A gives free education to 6–14-year-olds. (3) Right against Exploitation (Art. 23–24): no trafficking, begar or child labour. (4) Right to Freedom of Religion (Art. 25–28). (5) Cultural and Educational Rights (Art. 29–30): minorities may conserve culture and run institutions. (6) Right to Constitutional Remedies (Art. 32): approach the Supreme Court if rights are violated. They are justiciable but subject to reasonable restrictions.
